source.title: Unifying Count-Based Exploration and Intrinsic Motivation
source.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 29 (NeurIPS 2016)

confidence_rationale: The canonical RL-side instantiation of MECH-314a (novelty/count-based bonus): it derives a PSEUDOCOUNT from a density model so that count-based novelty generalises from the tabular case to high-dimensional non-tabular states, and shows a large exploration gain on Montezuma's Revenge. High source quality (NeurIPS, ~1300 citations). Supports MECH-314a's core mechanism (recency/rarity-of-encounter bonus) AND supplies the exact estimator REE needs to make a count-based bonus computable in a learned latent space rather than a tabular grid.
failure_signatures: The pseudocount is only as good as the density model: a poorly-fit or slowly-adapting density model gives mis-calibrated novelty, either over-rewarding already-seen states or failing to flag genuinely novel ones.

Count-based novelty is a LEVEL signal (rarity), not a derivative -- it shares MECH-314a's vulnerability to the noisy-TV / stochastic-trap failure Oudeyer & Kaplan flag: irreducibly random states stay perpetually 'novel' and can sink exploration budget.

The bonus decays as counts accumulate, so it drives COVERAGE (visit-everything) not COMPETENCE (achieve-goals); on Montezuma it helps reach new rooms but does not by itself teach robust goal-directed skill.

mapping.source_claim_statement: An exploration bonus of the form beta / sqrt(N(s)) -- classic count-based exploration -- can be generalised to non-tabular, high-dimensional state spaces by replacing the true visit count N(s) with a PSEUDOCOUNT derived from a learned density (sequential probability) model over states. The pseudocount is recovered from the model's prediction gain when a state is observed. This yields sensible per-state novelty from raw pixels and produces large exploration improvements on hard sparse-reward Atari games, notably Montezuma's Revenge.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-314a (novelty_bonus_striatal_analog) is REE's recency/rarity-of-encounter bonus, biologically anchored to ventral-striatal novelty (Wittmann 2008). Bellemare et al. supply its RL formalisation and, more usefully, the ESTIMATOR that lets REE compute it in a learned z-latent space (via a density model over z_world / z_resource) instead of tabular grid-cell counts -- the same generalisation step MECH-314a needs to move off a discrete CausalGridWorld tabulation onto the continuous latent substrate.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Two caveats. (1) REE's MECH-314a is currently a striatal-analog bonus; Bellemare's pseudocount presupposes a well-fit sequential density model over the state space, which REE has NOT built -- adopting it is a substrate ADD (a latent-space density model), not a re-description of the current substrate. (2) Count-based novelty is a LEVEL signal, so it inherits the noisy-TV trap and only drives coverage; it is the weakest of the three MECH-314 sub-flavours for the WS-1 competence problem (it visits, it does not master). It is complementary to -- not a substitute for -- MECH-314c learning-progress and the (unregistered) competence-based IM the goal pipeline needs.
mapping.source_context: Arcade Learning Environment (Atari 2600) from raw pixels; deep RL (DQN-family) agents. Structured deterministic-ish game dynamics; the Montezuma result is the field's standard sparse-reward exploration benchmark. Simulation only; no biological or REE substrate.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality very high (NeurIPS 2016, foundational, heavily cited). Mapping fidelity 0.70: the pseudocount mechanism maps cleanly onto MECH-314a's rarity bonus but requires a density-model substrate REE has not built. Transfer risk 0.35: Atari determinism differs from CausalGridWorld's stochasticity profile, and the coverage-not-competence limitation directly bears on why count-based novelty alone will not lift WS-1's floor.
